title: Northstar v. Meridian — defective laptops
label: Fictional demonstration • NS-2026-014
summary: A buyer receives 60 business laptops. Eighteen fail inspection, the supplier disputes the cause, and the buyer seeks repair or replacement and documented expenses. All parties, events and documents are fictional. This is an English UCC training scenario, not a real matter or a legal opinion.

exhibits.title: Purchase order
exhibits.text: Exhibit A — Northstar purchase order NS-2026-014. On 1 October 2026, Northstar Training Ltd ordered 60 new Meridian M14 business laptops from Meridian Devices Inc at USD 1,200 each, for USD 72,000 total. Northstar paid USD 36,000 as a deposit; USD 36,000 is stated to be due after delivery. The laptops must operate for ordinary office work and training, include 16 GB RAM and a 512 GB SSD, and pass a four-hour operating test. Delivery is due on 15 October 2026. The signed order says the seller will repair or replace confirmed defective units within ten business days after written notice. It contains no express disclaimer of merchantability and no exclusive-remedy clause. The order contains no choice-of-law or forum clause. This is a fictional transaction; the applicable jurisdiction must be established before any legal conclusion.

exhibits.title: Delivery receipt
exhibits.text: Exhibit B — Northstar delivery receipt NS-2026-014. Meridian delivered 60 laptop cartons on 15 October 2026. Northstar's warehouse clerk signed: Received 60 cartons; quantity only; equipment performance not tested. Six cartons had visible corner dents. No serial-number mapping between the dented cartons and individual devices was recorded. The delivery receipt does not establish when any device defect arose, whether a legal acceptance occurred, or whether any right was waived. This document is fictional.

exhibits.title: Inspection report
exhibits.text: Exhibit C — Northstar inspection report NS-2026-014. Northstar's technician tested all 60 Meridian M14 laptops on 17 October 2026. Twelve devices shut down within 30 minutes, and a different six devices could not charge. Eighteen distinct devices failed and 42 passed the test. All 60 devices matched the ordered RAM and SSD specifications. The report includes device serial numbers in a separate attachment that has not been supplied. The technician found no visible liquid damage but did not disassemble the devices. The report records symptoms, not a proven root cause. Repair cost and latent defects in the other 42 devices are not established. This document is fictional.

exhibits.title: Buyer notice
exhibits.text: Exhibit D — Northstar buyer notice NS-2026-014. On 20 October 2026, Northstar emailed Meridian reporting 18 failed laptops, attaching the inspection report and requesting repair or replacement under the purchase order. Northstar offered access to the failed units and asked Meridian to propose collection arrangements. Northstar wrote that the affected training class had been postponed. The sent-message copy is supplied, but proof of receipt is not. Northstar has not supplied a formal rejection notice, a revocation of acceptance, or evidence that the unpaid USD 36,000 balance was withheld lawfully. The legal effect and timeliness of the notice remain questions for analysis. This document is fictional.

exhibits.title: Supplier response
exhibits.text: Exhibit E — Meridian supplier response NS-2026-014. On 22 October 2026, Meridian acknowledged the complaint about 18 laptops. Meridian asserted that all units passed its factory testing and suggested transit damage or a buyer power-supply problem. No factory test records, carrier report or expert report accompanied the response. Meridian offered to inspect six sample units on 27 October 2026 but did not commit to repair or replacement by a specific date. The response does not resolve whether the defects existed at delivery. Meridian's asserted causes are disputed allegations, not established facts. This document is fictional.

exhibits.title: Loss schedule
exhibits.text: Exhibit F — Northstar loss schedule NS-2026-014. The 18 affected laptops have a contract price of USD 21,600, calculated as 18 times USD 1,200. Northstar lists USD 2,400 in temporary laptop hire and USD 900 in inspection expenses, both supported by fictional invoices in this exhibit: hire invoice NH-2400 and inspection invoice NI-900. Documented outlays total USD 3,300. Northstar also alleges USD 8,000 in lost profit, but supplies no bookings, margin calculation or mitigation evidence. Contract price, refund, repair cost and consequential loss are different measures and must not be added automatically or double-counted. The legal recoverability of any sum has not been established. This document is fictional.

questions.title: 1 · Find the core facts
questions.question: In the fictional Northstar NS-2026-014 case, how many Meridian M14 laptops failed inspection and what were the reported symptoms? Cite Exhibit C.
questions.check: Exhibit C reports 18 distinct failed units: 12 shutdowns and six charging failures. These are documented symptoms, not a proven cause.

questions.title: 2 · Build the timeline
questions.question: Build a dated timeline of the fictional Northstar NS-2026-014 dispute using Exhibits A through F. Cite the source for each event and distinguish sending notice from proving receipt.
questions.check: Compare 1, 15, 17, 20, 22 and 24 October. The supplied evidence does not establish when Meridian received the 20 October email.

questions.title: 3 · Compare disputed evidence
questions.question: Compare Exhibit C and Exhibit E in Northstar NS-2026-014. Which defects were observed, which causes are merely alleged, and which missing records would help resolve the dispute? Cite both exhibits.
questions.check: The inspection observed failures. Transit damage and power-supply problems are the supplier's unproven explanations. Request serial mapping, factory tests, carrier evidence and expert inspection.

questions.title: 4 · Find relevant law
questions.question: What does UCC 2-314 say about the implied warranty of merchantability and fitness for ordinary purposes? Retrieve and cite the statutory text.
questions.check: Open the Uniform Commercial Code § 2-314 evidence card. The bundled UCC is a reference snapshot; applicability to this fictional transaction still needs jurisdiction analysis.

questions.title: 5 · Check the numbers
questions.question: Using Exhibit A and Exhibit F of Northstar NS-2026-014, calculate the total order value, affected-unit contract value and documented additional outlays separately. Identify the unsupported lost-profit claim and avoid double counting. Cite the exhibits.
questions.check: Order USD 72,000; affected-unit contract value USD 21,600; documented outlays USD 3,300; unsupported alleged lost profit USD 8,000. These are not an automatic damages award.

questions.title: 6 · Draft a response
questions.question: Draft a professional response to Meridian for fictional matter NS-2026-014. Use the supplied case exhibits to request an inspection plan, factory records and a repair or replacement timetable. Separate supported facts from allegations, cite evidence, and do not assert a jurisdiction or legal entitlement not established by the record.
questions.check: A useful draft requests records and a timetable without inventing receipt dates, expert findings or a guaranteed remedy.

questions.title: 7 · Test missing information
questions.question: For Northstar NS-2026-014, what is the governing jurisdiction, the proven root cause of the failures and the exact legally recoverable damages? If the documents do not establish any of these, say so clearly and identify what further information is needed.
questions.check: None of the three is established by the case packet. A grounded response must not invent a court, jurisdiction, expert conclusion or final award.
